Reproduce the one-million-cell CRB artifacts

Xuesong Wang

12 September, 2026

Source: vignettes/million_cell_crb_artifacts.Rmd
million_cell_crb_artifacts.Rmd

Purpose

This vignette records exactly which public data are used for the one-million-cell CRB benchmark, how the data are transformed, where every artifact is stored, and how to reproduce both physical CRB codecs. It measures storage and I/O engineering behavior; the deterministic one-million-cell subset is not a new biological analysis cohort.

Source data

The source is the 10x Genomics 1M Neurons data set: E18 mouse brain nuclei processed by Cell Ranger 1.3.0. The public HDF5 matrix contains 1,306,127 cell barcodes and 27,998 features.

https://cf.10xgenomics.com/samples/cell-exp/1.3.0/1M_neurons/
  1M_neurons_filtered_gene_bc_matrices_h5.h5

The preparation script downloads this file without modifying it. The generated data do not live under the repository root. The repository contains the preparation and benchmark code, while the large source and derived artifacts live in an external user-cache directory.

Location Resolved path Relationship
Repository root /home/runner/work/CerebroNexus/CerebroNexus Git-tracked source, tests, and vignette only
Large-example cache root /home/runner/.cache/R/CerebroNexus/large-examples External to the repository; replaces <cache-root> below
One-million-cell data root /home/runner/.cache/R/CerebroNexus/large-examples/1m <cache-root>/1m/

By default, <cache-root> is file.path(tools::R_user_dir("CerebroNexus", "cache"), "large-examples"). On the recorded macOS host this resolves to /Users/nuioi/Library/Caches/org.R-project.R/R/CerebroNexus/large-examples/. Set CEREBRO_LARGE_CACHE to replace that complete cache-root path; for example, CEREBRO_LARGE_CACHE=/Volumes/FastSSD/cerebro-large-examples stores the dataset at /Volumes/FastSSD/cerebro-large-examples/1m/. A fresh run needs approximately 16 GiB of free space.

Processing steps

The transformation is deterministic:

  1. Open the public 10x HDF5 matrix with BPCells.
  2. Select exactly 1,000,000 barcodes at evenly spaced source indexes.
  3. Replace Ensembl row identifiers with unique gene_names symbols.
  4. Convert non-negative integer counts to BPCells uint32_t storage.
  5. Run NormalizeData() and FindVariableFeatures().
  6. Draw a 50,000-cell leverage-score sketch with seed 123.
  7. Run 30-component PCA, neighbours, clustering at resolution 1, and UMAP with seed 123 on the sketch.
  8. Project the PCA, cluster labels, and UMAP back to all 1,000,000 cells.
  9. Save a Seurat RDS plus its BPCells expression sidecar.
  10. Export counts, sample, seurat_clusters, and the full UMAP to a BPCells-backed CRB.
  11. Re-encode only the CRB control payload as thin RDS and thin qs2. Both files reuse the same unchanged Cerebro BPCells sidecar.

The thin CRB uses the sidecar’s ordered col_names as its canonical cell index. It omits the live expression handle, meta_data$cell_barcode, and projection barcode row names, records the col_names checksum, and restores those fields in readCerebro().

Files and formats

The following table is generated by the code in this vignette. exists and size_gib reflect the current cache; the file names, formats, and relative locations are fixed by the preparation workflow.

knitr::kable(artifact_table(), row.names = FALSE)

Seurat expression sidecar mouse_brain_1m.bpcells Expression matrix BPCells directory (uint32) FALSE NA seurat/mouse_brain_1m.bpcells

The resulting directory layout is relative to the external <cache-root>, not to <repository-root>:

<cache-root>/
└── 1m/
    ├── source/
    │   └── 1M_neurons_filtered_gene_bc_matrices_h5.h5
    ├── seurat/
    │   ├── mouse_brain_1m.rds
    │   └── mouse_brain_1m.bpcells/
    └── cerebro/
        ├── cerebro_mouse_brain_1m.crb
        ├── cerebro_mouse_brain_1m.bpcells/
        ├── cerebro_mouse_brain_1m_thin_rds.crb
        └── cerebro_mouse_brain_1m_thin_qs2.crb

.crb identifies the logical Cerebro data format, not the physical codec. Use readCerebro() for every new or old CRB. Direct readRDS() remains valid only for files explicitly written with codec = "rds" and legacy RDS CRBs.

Comparison against PR #165

The benchmark baseline is the legacy RDS CRB from PR #165 (69893a2b, CerebroNexus 4.4.3). The optimization branch is based directly on that merge commit and develops the CRB changes as CerebroNexus 4.5.0.

Recorded environment

Item Recorded value
Machine MacBook Pro (MacBookPro18,1)
CPU Apple M1 Pro, 10 cores (8 performance + 2 efficiency)
Memory 32 GiB
Storage Apple SSD AP1024R, 1 TB, APFS, Apple Fabric
Operating system macOS 27.0, build 26A5421a
Architecture arm64
R 4.6.1 (aarch64-apple-darwin23)
BPCells 0.3.1
qs2 0.2.2
Seurat / SeuratObject 5.5.1 / 5.4.0
Benchmark baseline PR #165 (69893a2b), CerebroNexus 4.4.3
Optimization candidate perf/pr0-million-cell-crb-qs2, based on PR #165 (69893a2b), CerebroNexus 4.5.0 development version

Measurements are warm-cache medians from five alternating rounds on the same unchanged BPCells sidecar. The benchmark loads the source checkout with pkgload::load_all(); the separately installed CerebroNexus 5.0.0 package is not used.

Write includes thin-payload compaction and serialization. Decode measures only physical deserialization. Hydrated read measures readCerebro(), including reopening the BPCells sidecar, validating its canonical cell index checksum, and restoring omitted metadata and projection row names.

Candidate Codec CRB size Write median Decode median Hydrated read median Size reduction vs PR #165 Write speedup Decode speedup Hydrated read speedup
PR #165 legacy CRB (69893a2b, v4.4.3) RDS 26.83 MiB 8001 ms 1296 ms 1479 ms — — — —
Thin CRB without qs2 (v4.5.0-dev) RDS 13.92 MiB 2947 ms 93 ms 356 ms 48.12% 2.71x 13.94x 4.15x
Thin CRB with qs2 (v4.5.0-dev) qs2 13.21 MiB 231 ms 41 ms 297 ms 50.75% 34.64x 31.61x 4.98x

Without qs2, thin CRB reduces the control file by 48.12%, accelerates writing by 2.71x, physical decoding by 13.94x, and hydrated readCerebro() by 4.15x relative to PR #165. With qs2, the reductions are 50.75%, 34.64x, 31.61x, and 4.98x respectively. The incremental file-size benefit of qs2 over thin RDS is only 5.07%; most of the size reduction therefore comes from removing redundant CRB fields rather than changing codec.

The checksum failure covered by the automated test is deliberately injected to prove that a CRB cannot silently attach the wrong BPCells sidecar. The genuine one-million-cell RDS and qs2 files used here both pass checksum validation.

The following command reruns all five alternating benchmark rounds and regenerates the source CSV used to record these measurements:

BASELINE=$(Rscript -e 'cat(file.path(tools::R_user_dir("CerebroNexus", "cache"), "large-examples", "1m", "cerebro", "cerebro_mouse_brain_1m.crb"))')
Rscript tests/bench/benchmark_million_cell_crb.R "$BASELINE" 5 tests/bench/results/million_cell_crb_pr165.csv

Run the complete preparation

The expensive chunks are disabled during ordinary package builds. Run the complete workflow from the repository root with:

CEREBRO_RUN_1M_VIGNETTE=true \
Rscript -e 'rmarkdown::render("vignettes/million_cell_crb_artifacts.Rmd")'

The following code performs the actual download, analysis, export, and codec conversion when CEREBRO_RUN_1M_VIGNETTE=true.

source(file.path(repo_root, "tests", "bench", "prepare_viewer_1m_data.R"))
pkgload::load_all(repo_root, quiet = TRUE)

source_crb <- prepareViewer1mBenchmarkData(cache_dir = cache_root)
object <- readCerebro(source_crb)
stopifnot(length(object$getCellNames()) == 1000000L)

saveCerebro(object, paths$thin_rds, codec = "rds")
saveCerebro(object, paths$thin_qs2, codec = "qs2")

Verify the outputs and regenerate the table

This final chunk reads both physical codecs through the same public API, checks their exact cell and UMAP ordering, and regenerates the artifact table from the files on disk.

expected_cells <- object$getCellNames()
expected_umap_cells <- rownames(object$getProjection("umap"))

for (path in c(paths$thin_rds, paths$thin_qs2)) {
  restored <- readCerebro(path)
  stopifnot(
    identical(restored$getCellNames(), expected_cells),
    identical(rownames(restored$getProjection("umap")), expected_umap_cells),
    identical(restored$meta_data$cell_barcode, expected_cells)
  )
  rm(restored)
  gc()
}

knitr::kable(artifact_table(), row.names = FALSE)

The BPCells directory is intentionally not copied for each codec. The RDS and qs2 .crb files contain alternative serializations of the same Cerebro control data and both point to cerebro_mouse_brain_1m.bpcells/.
